# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan, 2024: 1B.6 evidence note

Bottom line: I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that Sharif tolerated or encouraged proliferation by allies, proxies, clients, or domestic factions for short-term gain. The best available 2024 material points the other way, but it is mostly **institutional** rather than a direct ruler-level crackdown on a specific proliferator.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | Arms Control And Disarmament | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | Standing policy page; current version cites a May 2024 update | https://mofa.gov.pk/arms-control-and-disarmament | Pakistan’s official policy page says it supports CTBT objectives, a unilateral testing moratorium, FMCT negotiations, IAEA safeguards, reciprocal inspections proposals, UNSCR 1540 implementation, export controls, and non-discriminatory multilateral nonproliferation norms. This is the strongest general evidence that the government was resisting proliferation incentives rather than accommodating them. | 1B.6; also 1B.4, 1B.3 |
| Favorable | Pakistan and the UK held 6th Round of Dialogue on Arms Control and Non-Proliferation | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-05-16 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/6th-round-of-pakistan-uk-dialogue-on-arms-control-non-proliferation | Pakistan held a formal arms-control / nonproliferation dialogue with the UK and pledged continued coordination on UN, CD, IAEA, and OPCW issues. That supports a good-faith anti-proliferation posture. | 1B.6; also 1B.4 |
| Favorable | Pakistan-China Bilateral Consultations on Arms Control and Nonproliferation | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-09-14 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/pakistan-china-bilateral-consultations-on-arms-control-and-nonproliferation | Pakistan continued structured consultations on arms control and nonproliferation with China, including peaceful nuclear technology and multilateral treaty forums. This is evidence of resisting proliferation as a diplomatic norm, not enabling it. | 1B.6; also 1B.4 |
| Favorable | The visit of UN Disarmament Fellows to Pakistan | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-10-21 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/the-visit-of-un-disarmament-fellows-to-pakistan | Pakistan briefed UN disarmament fellows on arms control, disarmament, nonproliferation, and nuclear safety/security architecture. This is a concrete sign of public engagement with anti-proliferation norms. | 1B.6; also 1B.4, 1B.3 |
| Favorable | Message on the Occasion of Youm-e-Takbeer on 28th May 2024 | Press Information Department, Pakistan | 2024-05-27 | https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/25454 | The government described Pakistan as a responsible nuclear state committed to peaceful resolution of conflicts, stringent controls, comprehensive safety measures, and Credible Minimum Deterrence. That is compatible with rejecting proliferation-by-proxy logic. | 1B.6; also 1B.5, 1B.3 |
| Favorable | PM voices satisfaction over Pakistan Army’s operational preparedness | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-05 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/05-09-2024/pm-expresses-satisfaction-over-pak-armys-operational-preparedness | Sharif praised operational preparedness and described deterrence as preserving peace in nuclearized South Asia. This is not direct anti-proliferation evidence, but it supports a disciplined, non-proxy, non-escalatory posture. | 1B.6; also 1B.5 |
| Favorable | Pakistan's nuclear programme is for peaceful purposes: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-12-24 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/24-12-2024/pm-vows-to-root-out-scourge-of-terrorism | Sharif said Pakistan’s nuclear program is peaceful, defensive, and non-aggressive. This is direct restraint language, but still not evidence of a specific confrontation with a proliferating ally or faction. | 1B.6; also 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.5 |

## Search gap

- I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence that Sharif confronted a named ally, proxy, client, or domestic faction over proliferation.
- I also did **not** find credible 2024 evidence that he used proliferation as a political tool or tolerated it for short-term gain.
- So the best-supported conclusion is **general anti-proliferation posture, but no direct ruler-level case study** for 1B.6 in 2024. Confidence should stay low to moderate because the evidence is mostly institutional and indirect.
